channel.title: Canso Brief
channel.description: The podcast for the MLS 2028 mission. (Contact: dlindner16@hotmail.com)
channel.ns0:author: Derek Lindner

item.title: Episode 1 — The Launch Ecosystem: From Rockets to Revenue
item.description: The foundational module for the MLS 2028 curriculum. Explores the interconnected layers of the Canadian launch ecosystem — regulatory frameworks, physical infrastructure, market demand, and vehicle technology — and how they converge to make orbital access from Nova Scotia possible.

item.title: Ep02: The Regulatory Regime — Dissecting Bill C-28
item.description: A deep dive into the legal architecture of Canada's Space Launch Act (Bill C-28), exploring ministerial authority, site certification, and launch liability.

item.title: Episode 03: The Application Machine — Inside the Six-Review Web
item.description: A deep dive into the simultaneous coordination of Canada's regulatory reviews—from payload security to site safety—and how financial responsibility backstops the future of Canadian space launch.

item.title: Episode 04: The Minister's Two Questions
item.description: The Financial Responsibility Review and the Policy Review — the two places a Transport Canada decision comes down to a Minister's judgment call, not an engineering checklist. Examined through the newly signed Isar Aerospace-Maritime Launch Services facilities agreement at Spaceport Nova Scotia.

item.title: Episode 05: The Fence and the Cage
item.description: The Security Review and the Technology Security Review — one protects the launch site, the other protects treaty-controlled technology, and conflating them costs you credibility. Examined through the Canada-United States Technology Safeguards Agreement and the open questions around Isar Aerospace's Spectrum vehicle at Spaceport Nova Scotia.

item.title: Episode 06: Why Canso — The Geometry of Orbit
item.description: No equations, one globe: why inclination and launch latitude lock a satellite's reach at liftoff, why sun-synchronous orbits need a specific launch time, and why Canso is one of the only places in eastern North America where that geometry points at open ocean instead of populated land.

item.title: Episode 07: The Customs Desk for Orbit
item.description: Payload Review and Determination, Section 3.4 — the review that examines the actual cargo, and the two carve-outs (spectrum to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada; imaging to Global Affairs Canada) that define what it refuses to inspect. Why a transport regulator asks about satellite encryption, and what happens when you don't know your manifest yet.

item.title: Episode 08: The Thin Door
item.description: Safety Review, Part 1 of 7: why "a rocket is an aircraft" is the single sentence the entire regulatory regime hangs from, the five risk regimes and their measured quantities, and the surprising legal definitions of "public" and "casualty" that everything else is denominated in. Also: closing the deployed-payload ledger item carried over from Episode 07.
